L35: Sunflowers of Reed--Solomon Codes

L37: Authors: 【12†Roni Con】, 【13†Anina Gruica】, 【14†Maria Montanucci】, 【15†Ferdinando Zullo】
L38: Abstract: We introduce and study Reed--Solomon sunflowers, namely families of Reed--Solomon codes whose pairwise intersections are all equal to the same fixed subspace. This notion lies at the intersection of extremal subspace combinatorics and coding theory: it can be viewed as a structured version of the sunflower problem in t… ▽ More We introduce and study Reed--Solomon sunflowers, namely families of Reed--Solomon codes whose pairwise intersections are all equal to the same fixed subspace.
L39: This notion lies at the intersection of extremal subspace combinatorics and coding theory: it can be viewed as a structured version of the sunflower problem in the Grassmannian, and it naturally produces constant-dimension subspace codes with prescribed minimum distance. We focus mainly on the case in which the center is the one-dimensional space generated by the all-one vector.
L40: We give an algebraic criterion, expressed in terms of generalized $V$-matrices, ensuring that a family of Reed--Solomon codes forms such a sunflower. We then study the size of these families through counting and constructions. In dimension two, we show that all distinct Reed--Solomon codes form a sunflower and determine its size by counting Reed--Solomon codes up to affine equivalence of their evaluation vectors.
L41: For fixed dimension $k\geq3$ and length $\ell\geq2k-1$, we give an explicit recursive construction with $Ω_{k,\ell}(q^{\lfloor\ell/(2k-1)\rfloor})$ petals and a greedy existence argument with $Ω_{k,\ell}(q^{\ell-2k+2})$ petals as $q\to\infty$. We also apply the greedy argument to obtain families of $[\ell,k]_q$ MDS codes of size $Ω_{k,\ell}(q^{2(\ell-2k+2)})$, whose pairwise intersections have dimension at most one but need not be equal. △ Less

L42: # Thresholds and spread in set systems of bounded VC-dimension
L43: 
L44: Chong Shangguan ^{†}^{†}thanks: Research Center for Mathematics and Interdisciplinary Sciences, Shandong University, Qingdao 266237, China, and Frontiers Science Center for Nonlinear Expectations, Ministry of Education, Qingdao 266237, China. Email: theoreming@163.com.
L45: ###### Abstract
L46: Let $p_{c}(\mathcal{F})$, $q(\mathcal{F})$, and $q_{f}(\mathcal{F})$ denote the threshold, expectation threshold, and fractional expectation threshold of a family $\mathcal{F}$ of nonempty subsets of a finite set, respectively. We prove that there is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that, if $\mathcal{F}$ has VC dimension at most $d\geq 1$, then $p_{c}(\mathcal{F})\leq Cq(\mathcal{F})\log(d+1)$.
L47: More generally, for every $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$, a binomial random set of density $\min\{1,Cq(\mathcal{F})\log((d+1)/\varepsilon)\}$ contains a member of $\mathcal{F}$ with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$. Consequently, $q_{f}(\mathcal{F})\leq Cq(\mathcal{F})\log(d+1)$, verifying Talagrand’s integral–fractional conjecture for families of any fixed VC dimension.
L48: We also prove that if a $k$-spread probability measure has support of VC dimension at most $d$, then a binomial random set of density $\min\{1,(C/k)\log((d+1)/\varepsilon)\}$ contains a member of its support with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$. In both random-containment results, the factor $\log((d+1)/\varepsilon)$ is optimal up to absolute constants.
L49: As an application of the spread theorem, we prove that every $n$-uniform family of VC dimension at most $d$ with more than $(Cp^{-1}\log((d+1)/\varepsilon))^{n}$ members contains a $(p,\varepsilon)$-robust sunflower. In particular, every such family with more than $(Cr\log(d+1))^{n}$ members contains an $r$-sunflower, improving the recent bound $(Crd)^{n}$ of Ge, Wang, Xu, and Zhao.
L50: ## 1 Introduction
L51: 
L52: A basic problem in probabilistic combinatorics is to understand the threshold at which a random subset of a finite ground set contains a member of a prescribed set system. We briefly recall the necessary definitions and background; for more details, see the recent surveys [【30†14】, 【31†15】, 【32†17】, 【33†12】]. Throughout the paper, $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm, and $\log^{*}$ denotes the iterated logarithm.
L53: Let $U$ be a finite set, and write $W\sim\Bin(U,p)$ when each point of $U$ is included in $W$ independently with probability $p$. Let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{U}\setminus\{\varnothing\}$ be nonempty. Its threshold $p_{c}(\mathcal{F})$ is the unique $p$ such that $\mathop{\mathrm{Pr}}\nolimits_{W}[\exists S\in\mathcal{F}:S\subseteq W]=1/2$.
L54: For a family $\mathcal{G}\subseteq 2^{U}$, the span of $\mathcal{G}$ is $\langle\mathcal{G}\rangle=\{A\subseteq U:\exists T\in\mathcal{G},\ T\subseteq A\}$. We say that $\mathcal{G}$ covers $\mathcal{F}$ if $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\langle\mathcal{G}\rangle$. If $\mathcal{G}$ covers $\mathcal{F}$, then every $W$ containing a member of $\mathcal{F}$ contains a member of $\mathcal{G}$. Hence $\mathop{\mathrm{Pr}}\nolimits_{W}[\exists S\in\mathcal{F}:S\subseteq W]\leq\sum_{T\in\mathcal{G}}p^{|T|}$.

L26: ###### Abstract
L27: A sunflower with $p$ petals consists of $p$ sets whose pairwise intersections are identical. The goal of the sunflower problem is to find the smallest $r=r(p,k)$ such that any family of $r^{k}$ distinct $k$-element sets contains a sunflower with $p$ petals. Building upon a breakthrough of Alweiss, Lovett, Wu and Zhang from 2019, Rao proved that $r=O(p\log(pk))$ suffices; this bound was reproved by Tao in 2020.
L28: In this short note we record that $r=O(p\log k)$ suffices, by using a minor variant of the probabilistic part of these recent proofs.
L29: ## 1 Introduction
L30: A sunflower with $p$ petals is a family of $p$ sets whose pairwise intersections are identical (the intersections may be empty). Let $\mathrm{Sun}(p,k)$ denote the smallest natural number $s$ with the property that any family of at least $s$ distinct $k$-element sets contains a sunflower with $p$ petals.
L31: In 1960, Erdős and Rado [【9†4】] proved that ${(p-1)^{k}}<{\mathrm{Sun}(p,k)}\leq{(p-1)^{k}k!+1}=O((pk)^{k})$, and conjectured that for any $p\geq 2$ there is a constant ${C_{p}>0}$ such that ${\mathrm{Sun}(p,k)\leq C_{p}^{k}}$ for all $k\geq 2$. This famous conjecture in extremal combinatorics was one of Erdős’ favorite problems [【10†2】], for which he offered a $1000 reward [【11†3】]; it remains open despite considerable attention [【12†7】].
L32: In 2019, there was a breakthrough on the sunflower conjecture: using iterative encoding arguments, Alweiss, Lovett, Wu and Zhang [【13†1】] proved that ${\mathrm{Sun}(p,k)\leq(Cp^{3}\log k\log\log k)^{k}}$ for some constant $C>0$, opening the floodgates for further improvements. Using Shannon’s noiseless coding theorem, Rao [【14†8】] subsequently simplified their proof and obtained a slightly better bound.
L33: Soon thereafter, Frankston, Kahn, Narayanan and Park [【15†5】] refined some key counting arguments from [【13†1】]. Their ideas were then utilized by Rao [【16†9】] to improve the best-known sunflower bound to ${\mathrm{Sun}(p,k)\leq(Cp\log(pk))^{k}}$ for some constant $C>0$, which in 2020 was reproved by Tao in his blog [【17†10】] using Shannon entropy arguments.
L34: The aim of this short note is to record, for the convenience of other researchers, that a minor variant of (the probabilistic part of) the arguments from [【16†9】, 【17†10】] gives ${\mathrm{Sun}(p,k)\leq(Cp\log k)^{k}}$ for some constant $C>0$.
L35: ###### Theorem 1.
L36: 
L37: There is a constant $C\geq 4$ such that $\mathrm{Sun}(p,k)\leq(Cp\log k)^{k}$ for all integers $p,k\geq 2$.
L38: Setting $r(p,k)=Cp\log k+\mathbbm{1}_{\{{k=1}\}}p$, we shall in fact prove ${\mathrm{Sun}(p,k)\leq r(p,k)^{k}}$ for all integers $p\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$. Similarly to the strategy of [【13†1】, 【16†9】, 【17†10】], this upper bound follows easily by induction on $k\geq 1$ from Lemma 【18†2】 below, where a family $\mathcal{S}$ of $k$-element sets is called $r$-spread if there are at most $r^{k-|T|}$ sets of $\mathcal{S}$ that contain any non-empty set $T$.
L39: (Indeed, the base case $k=1$ is trivial due to $r(p,1)=p$, and the induction step $k\geq 2$ uses a simple case distinction: if $\mathcal{S}$ is $r(p,k)$-spread, then Lemma 【18†2】 guarantees a sunflower with $p$ petals; otherwise there is a non-empty set $T$ such that more than $r(p,k)^{k-|T|}\geq r(p,k-|T|)^{k-|T|}$ sets of $\mathcal{S}$ contain $T$, and among this family of sets we easily find a sunflower with $p$ petals using induction.)
L40: ###### Lemma 2.
L41: 
L42: There is a constant $C\geq 4$ such that, setting $r(p,k)=Cp\log k$, the following holds for all integers $p,k\geq 2$. If a family $\mathcal{S}$ with ${|\mathcal{S}|\geq r(p,k)^{k}}$ sets of size $k$ is $r(p,k)$-spread, then $\mathcal{S}$ contains $p$ disjoint sets.
L43: Inspired by [【13†1】], in [【16†9】, 【17†10】] probabilistic arguments are used to deduce Lemma 【18†2】 with $r(p,k)=\Theta(p\log(pk))$ from Theorem 【19†3】 below, where $X_{\delta}$ denotes the random subset of $X$ in which each element is included independently with probability $\delta$.
L44: ###### Theorem 3 (Main technical estimate of [【16†9】, 【17†10】]).
L45: 
L46: There is a constant $B\geq 1$ such that the following holds for any integer ${k\geq 2}$, any reals ${0<\delta,\epsilon\leq 1/2}$, ${r\geq B\delta^{-1}\log(k/\epsilon)}$, and any family $\mathcal{S}$ of $k$-element subsets of a finite set $X$. If $\mathcal{S}$ is $r$-spread with $|\mathcal{S}|\geq r^{k}$, then ${\operatorname{\mathbb{P}{}}(\exists S\in\mathcal{S}:S\subseteq X_{\delta})}>{1-\epsilon}$. ∎

L27: #### Limitations of the slice rank method in additive combinatorics

L39: 【20†additive combinatorics】, 【21†arithmetic progression free sets】, 【22†slice rank】, 【23†Sunflower conjecture】, 【24†tensor】

L41: Abstract:
L42: The slice rank method gives exponential bounds for sets with no three-term arithmetic progression in finite vector spaces of odd characteristic and for three-sunflower-free families of subsets of a fixed ground set. We show that for $k\ge4$, every tensor that is nonzero exactly on the $k$-term arithmetic progression relation or the $k$-sunflower relation has maximal slice rank over every coefficient field.
L43: When the support is prescribed only on pairwise distinct inputs, we obtain comparable lower bounds, which likewise rule out exponential savings.
